event.text:
Implemented the adaptive shared property-row behavior in the Details tree at the shared UI layer, so it applies generically to all `showLabel` property controls (not field-name specific).

### What changed

- Updated `Label` in `elements/ui/index.tsx` (the shared property-row primitive used by Sketchpad details rows).
- Kept the default inline layout (`label | value control`) as the baseline.
- Added runtime adaptive switching to stacked mode using measured layout constraints:
  - Observes row/label/control size changes with `ResizeObserver`.
  - Detects “too narrow / collision risk” via:
    - actual overlap check (`labelRect.right` vs `controlRect.left`)
    - minimum required inline width (`label scrollWidth + control scrollWidth + gap`) vs available row width.
  - Switches to stacked mode only when needed.
- In stacked mode:
  - first line is still the tree gutter + label flow,
  - second line is the value control in normal document flow, offset to the value-side column start.
- Preserved existing tree primitives and structure:
  - `TreeSection`, `TreeItem`, `TreeRow`, `TreeContent`, `IndentationLines`
  - hierarchy, branch lines, spacing rhythm, actions
- No absolute positioning hacks or field-specific width hacks were introduced.

### Verification

- Ran UI tests: `npm test` in `elements/ui`
  - `36 passed`
- Ran lints on edited file:
  - `ReadLints` on `elements/ui/index.tsx` returned no errors.

event.text:
Adjusted both issues in the shared property-row layout logic (`elements/ui/index.tsx`).

### Fixes applied

- **Value column alignment fixed**
  - In stacked mode, the control row now offsets by **label width + inline gap** (`96 + 8`) so it lines up exactly with the normal value column.
  - This resolves the “input value not matching the rest” misalignment.

- **Stopped row jumping (inline ↔ stacked oscillation)**
  - Added a **hysteresis threshold** for stacked → inline transition (`24px` buffer).
  - Behavior now:
    - switch to stacked as soon as collision/tight width is detected,
    - only switch back to inline when there is clearly enough width.
  - This removes the flicker/jump between first and second row and keeps it stable on the bottom row when space is tight.

### Validation

- Ran `npm test` in `elements/ui`: all tests pass (`36/36`).
- Checked lints on `elements/ui/index.tsx`: no linter errors.
